name: Before/after image compare, clip-path split driven by a native range input
notes: Original library pattern, not pulled from a client build. The interaction is the before/after drag used on Yardzen project stories: one frame, a vertical seam, labels on each side. Implemented with CSS clip-path and a real range input so keyboard, touch, and screen readers come from the browser. The script only writes --val. Images are drawn diagrams (assets/placeholders/compare-before.svg and compare-after.svg), stamped as placeholders, because a before/after made of two unrelated stock photos would imply a job that did not happen. The house, clouds, and stamp are identical in both files so the seam does not jump; only the yard changes. Swap both for a real pair of the same crop before shipping, and if this is the hero set the top image to loading=eager. --thumb is 44px and must match the knob. 0 and 100 stop half a knob in from the edge so the handle stays on the picture. Without the script the split stays at 50/50. The drag is user-controlled, so prefers-reduced-motion does not remove it. Theme --brand.
